headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of new grid infrastructure required to serve their high demand, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger's administration
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Governor Urges SCC: Data Centers Must Pay for Infrastructure
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger urged the State Corporation Commission (SCC) to require data centers to cover the cost of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for them. This decision aims to save Virginia families and small businesses hundreds of millions of dollars by preventing these costs from being passed on to other ratepayers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report the total volume of water supplied to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing critical data for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Data Center Water Use Tracking
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers. This legislation aims to strengthen water-use reporting and provide better data for understanding the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources, especially as data centers expand.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data centers, environmental advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Siting Law Explained
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct noise studies for homes and schools within 500 feet of a proposed site. While it mandates studies and allows localities to assess other impacts like water and historic resources, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local authorities.
